summaries.title: 62e vergadering, donderdag 9 april 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 62nd parliamentary session on April 9, 2026, focused primarily on energy transition and housing policy, with 101 topics discussed and 75 decisions made. Key debates centered on heat pump implementation mandates, national insulation programs for vulnerable households, rental market regulation, and the balance between sustainability requirements and administrative burden on citizens and businesses. Multiple motions were put forward by opposition and coalition parties, with outcomes ranging from government approval to parliament's discretion.
topics: Heat Pump Implementation and Hybrid Heating Systems
National Isolation Program and Collective Insulation Approaches
Complaint Procedure Abolition for Rental Disputes

summaries.title: 61e vergadering, woensdag 8 april 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 61st parliamentary session on April 8, 2026 addressed 71 topics with 63 decisions, focusing heavily on AI strategy and employment protection alongside infrastructure and port management issues. Key debates centered on balancing AI development ambitions with worker protections, while multiple motions on maritime infrastructure and port security were approved or conditionally accepted.
topics: Port Security and Foreign Interference Prevention
Scenarios for Reduced Fossil Fuel Handling in Ports

summaries.title: 60e vergadering, dinsdag 7 april 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 60th parliamentary session of April 7, 2026 addressed 78 topics with 93 decisions, spanning education policy, spatial planning, energy security, and language guidelines. Key debates centered on the controversial OCW language guide, school truancy prevention legislation, kerosene supply crisis planning, and fireworks compensation regulations. The session demonstrated broad coalition consensus on education and spatial planning measures, while revealing significant ideological divisions over language policy between right-wing parties and the government.
topics: OCW Language Guide and Inclusive Language Policy
School Truancy Prevention Law (Wet terugdringen schoolverzuim)

summaries.title: 59e vergadering, donderdag 2 april 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 59th Dutch parliamentary session on April 2, 2026 focused primarily on prison system crisis management, with 69 topics debated and 70 decisions made. Key disputes centered on tablet distribution to detainees, transgender placement policies, and broader prison capacity solutions, revealing significant disagreement between right-wing coalition partners (PVV, VVD) and the government over security measures and legal compliance. The government committed to presenting an action plan before summer recess while defending its tablet pilot program and opposing several opposition motions.

summaries.title: 58e vergadering, woensdag 1 april 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 58th parliamentary session on April 1, 2026, focused extensively on addressing the Netherlands' teacher shortage crisis, with 77 topics discussed and 70 decisions made. Multiple parties proposed varied solutions ranging from hybrid teaching models and lateral entry programs to pedagogical reforms and structural investigations. Significant disagreements emerged between parties on whether the shortage is inevitable or a result of political choices, and on the most effective intervention strategies.
topics: School Management Structure and Professional Autonomy
Lateral Entry Programs and Return Guarantees
Municipal Funding and Structural Budget Gaps

summaries.title: 57e vergadering, dinsdag 31 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 57th Dutch parliamentary session on March 31, 2026 addressed major geopolitical and domestic policy challenges, with heated debates over US weapons reallocation potentially affecting Ukraine aid, significant concerns about child protection system failures, and immigration law amendments. The government faced sustained pressure from opposition parties demanding stronger European defense autonomy, clearer commitments on Ukraine support, and more aggressive action on child welfare reforms.
topics: Pentagon Weapons Reallocation from Ukraine to Middle East

summaries.title: 56e vergadering, donderdag 26 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 56th Dutch parliamentary session on March 26, 2026 addressed a critical housing affordability crisis with 80 topics debated and 93 decisions made. Central disputes emerged between coalition and opposition parties over the timing and scope of reforms to the Affordable Housing Act, with particular tension over middle-segment rental housing decline, construction regulatory simplification, and mortgage lending policies. Deep ideological divisions surfaced regarding migration's role in housing demand, reflecting broader coalition fragmentation on this contentious issue.
topics: Construction Decree and Building Regulations Simplification
Housing Affordability and Rental Market Crisis
Mortgage Lending Reform and Property Price Effects

summaries.title: 55e vergadering, woensdag 25 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 55th Dutch parliamentary session on March 25, 2026 focused on a contentious bill regarding digital municipal council meetings. The central debate pitted those advocating for strict legal definitions limiting digital meetings to crisis situations against those favoring local autonomy with vaguer 'special circumstances' criteria. After extensive debate involving 100 topics and resulting in 77 decisions, significant amendments were proposed to clarify when physical meetings can be replaced by digital alternatives.
topics: Definition and Scope of 'Bijzondere Omstandigheden' (Special Circumstances)
Trust in Local Government vs. Risk of Political Misuse
Democratic Principle: Physical vs. Digital Meetings

summaries.title: 54e vergadering, dinsdag 24 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 54th parliamentary session on March 24, 2026 was dominated by heated debates over social housing allocation for status holders (asylum beneficiaries) and immigration policy, with 95 topics discussed and 104 decisions made. The government withdrew a law banning preferential housing treatment for status holders while committing to alternative solutions by end-2026, triggering strong opposition from PVV and other parties who view this as discriminatory to Dutch citizens. Additional debates covered agriculture, environmental policy, weapons exports to Israel, and asylum center agreements.
topics: Status Holders' Preferential Access to Social Housing
Agriculture, Nature, and Animal Welfare Policy

summaries.title: 53e vergadering, donderdag 19 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 53rd Dutch parliamentary meeting on March 19, 2026 focused primarily on the nitrogen crisis resolution strategy, with Minister Van Essen presenting a comprehensive three-pronged approach backed by 20 billion euros through 2035. The debate revealed significant tension between the government's compliance-focused strategy and opposition parties' concerns about farmer welfare, rural deprivation, and property rights implications.

summaries.title: 52e vergadering, dinsdag 17 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 52nd Dutch parliamentary session on March 17, 2026 focused predominantly on responding to recent terrorist attacks on Jewish institutions in Rotterdam and Amsterdam, with 51 topics addressed and 93 decisions made. Parliament debated root causes of antisemitism, security measures, and broader threats to democratic institutions, with broad consensus on strengthening protections while addressing systemic antisemitism through education and cultural initiatives. Multiple action plans were adopted concerning traffic safety, political security, and support for democratic resilience.

summaries.title: 51e vergadering, donderdag 12 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 51st Dutch parliamentary session on March 12, 2026, focused heavily on international military conflict, particularly US and Israeli attacks on Iran. The meeting revealed significant divisions between left-wing parties opposing military intervention as illegal and violating international law, and right-wing parties supporting defensive military action, while the government maintained a cautious middle position of 'understanding' rather than direct support for offensive operations.
topics: International Military Conflict and International Law
Dutch Military Deployment to the Region
International Governance and United Nations Reform

summaries.title: 50e vergadering, woensdag 11 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 50th parliamentary session of March 11, 2026 focused on a comprehensive debate of the 2026 Social Affairs budget, featuring intense discussion of the cabinet's proposed welfare reforms including unemployment insurance (WW) cuts, pension age increases, and wage reductions affecting approximately 260,000 workers. The session revealed significant coalition tensions between reform-minded ministers and opposition parties, with GroenLinks-PvdA and SP mounting strong criticism of dismantling post-war social protections, while coalition partners like D66 set conditions for supporting implementation.
topics: Worker Protection and Unemployment Insurance (WW) Cuts
Wajong (Disabled Youth Benefit) Guarantee Amount Cuts
Social Security Governance and Worker-Employer Control
European Social Fund and Local Government Partnership Plans

summaries.title: 49e vergadering, dinsdag 10 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 49th parliamentary session on March 10, 2026 addressed a cost-of-living crisis driven by escalating fuel prices (€2.45-€2.52/liter with potential rise to €3), alongside significant policy discussions on paternity recognition fraud, digital security, and platform regulation. The government adopted a cautious, evidence-based approach to fuel price intervention while committing to concrete measures on immigration fraud and media oversight, resulting in 82 decisions across 96 topics debated.
topics: Rising Fuel Prices and Cost of Living Crisis
Media Commissioner and Political Advertisement Monitoring
Digital Security, Data Protection, and Cable Infrastructure

summaries.title: 48e vergadering, donderdag 5 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 48th parliamentary session on March 5, 2026 focused primarily on Healthcare System Reform, with 129 topics discussed and 109 decisions reached. Minister Hermans presented the government's healthcare transformation plan emphasizing prevention and sustainability through structural reforms including higher own-risk contributions and user fees, while opposition parties, particularly GroenLinks-PvdA and SP, strongly criticized the approach as counterproductive and questioned whether cost-control measures would create barriers to necessary care. The session also addressed vaccination policy, disability care, and nicotine product regulations, with the cabinet agreeing to seek broader parliamentary input on implementation details.

summaries.title: 47e vergadering, woensdag 4 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 47th Dutch parliamentary session on March 4, 2026, focused primarily on the Selibon waste management crisis in Bonaire, where serious environmental and health violations have persisted despite years of intervention attempts. Parliament achieved broad cross-party consensus on urgent action, approving multiple motions for RIVM air quality monitoring, implementation of Ombudsman recommendations, and regional waste cooperation, while the government sought additional time for coordinating relocation plans and budget allocations. Additional discussion covered island council expansion and portfolio transitions between ministries.
topics: Selibon Waste Management Crisis in Bonaire

summaries.title: 46e vergadering, dinsdag 3 maart 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 46th Dutch Parliamentary session on March 3, 2026 was dominated by sharp criticism of the cabinet's cautious initial response to US and Israeli military actions against Iran. While the government secured KLM cooperation for evacuating stranded Dutch citizens and committed to energy price mitigation measures, multiple parties across the political spectrum attacked Prime Minister Jetten's emphasis on restraint and international law as insufficiently supportive of allies and failing to address the Iranian regime's brutality.
topics: Cabinet's Initial Response to Iran Strikes
Evacuation of Dutch Citizens from Middle East
Energy Price Mitigation and Supply Security

summaries.title: 45e vergadering, donderdag 26 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 45th Dutch parliamentary session on February 26, 2026 focused on government cooperation strategies and the new coalition cabinet's approach to major policy challenges. Prime Minister Jetten outlined a four-part thematic framework for addressing parliamentary concerns and emphasized early stakeholder consultation, while significant tension emerged around pension reform (AOW), public trust deficits (66% lack confidence), and the government's willingness to genuinely modify proposals based on opposition and civil society input.
topics: AOW (Old Age Pension) reform and labor relations

summaries.title: 44e vergadering, woensdag 25 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 44th parliamentary session on February 25, 2026, focused on the newly formed minority government cabinet led by Prime Minister Jetten and the major policy reforms it intends to implement. The meeting revealed significant tensions between the coalition and opposition regarding welfare reforms, environmental targets, and healthcare cuts, while both sides emphasized the need for a new political culture based on genuine cooperation rather than partisan maneuvering.
topics: Trust in Democracy and Political Culture

summaries.title: 43e vergadering, donderdag 12 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 43rd parliamentary session on February 12, 2026 addressed major fiscal and energy policy reforms, including the contentious Box 3 wealth tax implementation and urgent measures to address energy affordability and grid infrastructure challenges. With 81 topics debated and 70 decisions made, the session reflected significant disagreements between progressive parties advocating for stronger wealth taxation and conservative parties opposing tax increases, while energy policy discussions centered on balancing affordability, sustainability, and infrastructure investment.
topics: Box 3 Wealth Tax Reform (Wet werkelijk rendement box 3)
Energy Affordability and Household Energy Costs
Grid Infrastructure Crisis and TenneT Network Congestion
Gas Storage and Energy Security Strategy
Banking Crisis Framework (Wet nadere uitvoering BRRD-implementatie)

summaries.title: 42e vergadering, woensdag 11 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 42nd parliamentary session on February 11, 2026 addressed 82 topics with 75 decisions made, spanning education policy, LGBTIQ+ youth attitudes, and labor negotiations. Key debates centered on transparency in education collective bargaining negotiations, declining youth acceptance of LGBTIQ+ persons, and education system adequacy in the Caribbean Netherlands. The session reflected tensions between government confidentiality concerns and parliamentary demands for transparency and comprehensive policy responses.
topics: Confidential Information Sharing for Education Collective Bargaining (CAO)
Education System Appropriateness in Caribbean Netherlands
Education as Investment and Broad Welfare Measurement

summaries.title: 41e vergadering, dinsdag 10 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: Deze plenaire vergadering werd gedomineerd door de eerste termijn van de begrotingsbehandeling Klimaat en Groene Groei, waarin het nieuwe coalitieakkoord van D66, CDA en VVD uitgebreid ter discussie stond: linkse partijen vonden het te weinig ambitieus en te fossiel, rechtse partijen vonden het te duur en te weinig realistisch. Tijdens het vragenuur kwamen drie actuele kwesties aan bod: een ondergedoken politieagent na een aanhouding in Utrecht, asbest in speelzand voor kinderen en slechte naleving van bestrijdingsmiddelenregels door snijbloementelers, waarbij bewindspersonen weinig harde toezeggingen deden. In meerdere tweeminutendebatten over kernenergie, gaswinning, gasvoorraden en de COP30-top werden tientallen moties ingediend en van een kabinetsoordeel voorzien. Bij de stemmingen werden veel moties over de begrotingen Water, Jeugd, Binnenlandse Zaken en Asiel en Migratie aangenomen of verworpen, en werd de stemming over amendementen bij de Wet werkelijk rendement box 3 uitgesteld naar donderdag. Twee nieuwe Kamerleden, mevrouw Van Oosterhout (GroenLinks-PvdA) en de heer Van den Berg (JA21), hielden hun maidenspeech.
topics: Begroting Klimaat en Groene Groei 2026: toetsing van het nieuwe coalitieakkoord
Vragenuur: ondergedoken politieagent na aanhouding onder het Bollendak in Utrecht
Vragenuur: asbest in speelzand voor kinderen
Vragenuur: lage naleving gewasbeschermingsmiddelen bij snijbloementelers
Stemmingen over moties bij de begrotingen Water, Jeugd, Binnenlandse Zaken en Asiel en Migratie

summaries.title: 40e vergadering, donderdag 5 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 40th parliamentary meeting of February 5, 2026, focused on protecting Dutch local officials from intimidation and threats while addressing municipal budget challenges. The session resulted in 42 decisions, including €3 million allocated for council meeting security measures and €3 billion for municipalities to address rising costs in youth care, alongside rejections of several amendments regarding political party financing, anti-discrimination work, and ProDemos funding.
topics: Protection of Democracy and Local Officials
Municipal Budget Support and Rising Costs
AI Pilot Program for Freedom of Information (Woo)

summaries.title: 39e vergadering, woensdag 4 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 39th parliamentary session on February 4, 2026, addressed 109 topics with 116 decisions, focusing primarily on local government strengthening, regional cooperation funding, and administrative reform. Key debates centered on removing barriers for benefit recipients in local politics, clarifying financing for regional development programs, and implementing government efficiency measures. While several motions were appreciated by the government, tensions emerged between parliamentary ambitions and fiscal constraints.
topics: Strengthening Local Government - Support for Benefit Recipients
Online Hate Speech and Digital Security

summaries.title: 38e vergadering, dinsdag 3 februari 2026
summaries.summaryText: On February 3, 2026, the Dutch parliament held its 38th session to debate the coalition agreement of a three-party government formed by D66, VVD, and CDA, with D66 leader Jetten as Prime Minister. The 76 decisions covered major policy reforms including healthcare changes, defense spending increases, pension age adjustments, and tax measures, with significant opposition from PVV and GroenLinks-PvdA over fiscal burden distribution and broken campaign promises.

summaries.title: 37e vergadering, donderdag 29 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 37th parliamentary session on January 29, 2026 addressed 115 topics with 108 decisions made. The meeting was dominated by intensive scrutiny of the Dutch criminal justice system's chronic case processing delays, with parliament demanding urgent structural reforms through a comprehensive 'delta plan' while the Minister of Justice advocated for incremental improvements within existing frameworks. Multiple other Justice and Security matters were debated and approved, revealing broader tensions between parliamentary oversight demands and ministerial operational autonomy.
topics: Criminal Justice Chain Performance and Case Processing Delays
Police Participation in Halal Village Festival
Data-Sharing Issues in Traffic Fines and Multi-Problem Family Cases

summaries.title: 36e vergadering, woensdag 28 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 36th parliamentary session of January 28, 2026 addressed 96 topics with 74 decisions, focusing primarily on online fraud prevention, police conduct and neutrality policies, and public safety measures. Key debates centered on establishing centralized fraud reporting systems, regulating police operational procedures including selection tools and religious attire policies for civil enforcement officers, and strengthening victim protection mechanisms across multiple domains.

summaries.title: 35e vergadering, dinsdag 27 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 35th parliamentary session of January 27, 2026 addressed 60 topics with 49 decisions, focusing primarily on the Belgian toll vignette dispute and domestic policy matters including school safety, datacenter regulation, and payment systems legislation. Minister Tieman committed to formal negotiations with Belgian authorities on the €100 toll vignette while consulting regional stakeholders, while broader debates revealed tensions between European integration and national economic protection.
topics: Digital Sovereignty and American Tech Dominance

summaries.title: 34e vergadering, donderdag 22 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 34th parliamentary session on January 22, 2026, addressed 94 topics with 75 decisions, focusing heavily on infrastructure challenges and housing development. Key discussions centered on shared mobility standards, critical infrastructure funding needs, and several urgent regional crises including Terschelling harbor access and bridge/tunnel solutions in the Netherlands.

summaries.title: 33e vergadering, woensdag 21 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 33rd parliamentary session of January 21, 2026, focused primarily on economic policy and innovation, with 85 topics discussed and 55 decisions made. Three key motions on start-up support were unanimously approved, including commitments to improve IP deal terms, secure employee participation schemes, and fund academic valorization. The session also initiated budget debates on the Ministry of Economic Affairs and National Growth Fund, revealing coalition tensions over R&D investment financing and the role of public versus private investment.
topics: Regulatory Burden Reduction and Business Support
AI Innovation and Worker Protection Balance

summaries.title: 32e vergadering, dinsdag 20 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 32nd Dutch parliamentary session on January 20, 2026 addressed 54 topics and made 48 decisions, with major focus on caregiver support, youth suicide prevention, and EU trade policy response. Key commitments included establishing national minimum standards for caregiver support, launching a 2027 research program on youth suicide causes, and coordinating EU response to Trump tariffs at an emergency Council meeting.
topics: EU Trade Response to Trump Tariffs

summaries.title: 31e vergadering, donderdag 15 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 31st parliamentary meeting of January 15, 2026 focused extensively on housing policy, with Minister Keijzer presenting achievements from the December 2024 Woontop (Housing Summit) and outlining progress toward increasing annual housing production from 75,000 to 100,000 units. The meeting addressed multiple housing-related challenges including vacation park legalization, housing corporation financing crises, rent increase policies, and regulatory reform, resulting in 5 formal motions and several ministerial commitments for the incoming cabinet.
topics: Housing Construction Progress and Woontop Outcomes
Vacation Parks and Recreational Housing Legalization
Rent Increases and Service Costs Burden
Municipal Housing Quotas and Status Holder Preference
Breakthrough and Large-Scale Housing Locations Implementation
Homelessness Prevention and Zero Homelessness 2030 Goal
EU Housing Act Amendments and State Aid Exemptions

summaries.title: 30e vergadering, woensdag 14 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The 30th parliamentary session on January 14, 2026 focused primarily on Dutch arms export policy, with 85 topics debated and 59 decisions reached. Key debates centered on weapons embargoes against Israel and Sudan, export controls, and humanitarian aid policy, with the government maintaining a case-by-case assessment approach against opposition calls for blanket restrictions. Multiple motions on strict export limitations were advised against, while measures on Sudan weapons diversion were referred to parliament for further consideration.
topics: Dual-use Goods and EU Export Harmonization
Dutch Dependence on Israeli Weapons Industry

summaries.title: 29e vergadering, dinsdag 13 januari 2026
summaries.summaryText: The Dutch Parliament held an extensive debate on January 13, 2026, regarding severe violence against emergency responders during New Year's Eve, with 64 topics discussed and 38 decisions made. The government committed to a national firework ban by August 1, 2026, enhanced sentencing enforcement, international coordination on firework restrictions, and a comprehensive evaluation of the incidents. The debate revealed significant disagreement between parties on root causes, with conservatives blaming permissive policies while progressive parties emphasized the need for enforcement and societal measures.
topics: Violence Against Emergency Responders During New Year's Eve
Criminal Justice Response and Sentencing Enhancement
Police and Emergency Services Equipment and Support
Mohamed Baajour Case and Public Order Management
